blocks.text: Essential Excel shortcuts for logistics planners

Speed is vital when you are managing hundreds of rows of shipment data. On a Mac, you can save significant time by learning the right key combinations. Use ⌘ + T to quickly turn a range of cells into a formal table. This makes sorting and filtering your logistics data much easier. Use ⌃ + Space to select an entire column and ⇧ + Space to select a row. These small actions add up over a busy day of planning routes and monitoring inventory levels.
Managing large datasets on your Mac

Logistics planning often involves massive spreadsheets. Excel for Mac handles up to 1,048,576 rows. Keep your files fast by avoiding unnecessary formatting on empty cells. If your sheet slows down, try to convert data ranges into official tables. Use Data > Filter to manage your views without deleting rows. If you need to compare two lists of carriers, use the XLOOKUP function instead of older methods. It is faster and more reliable for large datasets.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to show you where the Filter button is if you get lost in a large sheet. Lazur will draw a circle around the correct icon in the ribbon.
blocks.title: Find tools fast

blocks.text: Errors in shipping codes or delivery dates can cause major disruptions. Use the Data Validation feature to restrict what can be typed into specific cells. Go to Data > Data Validation to set up dropdown lists for carrier names or status codes. This ensures that everyone on your team enters data in the same format. It saves you from cleaning up typos later in the week.

Pivot tables are your best friend for summarizing delivery performance. Select your data range and go to Insert > PivotTable to get started. You can quickly see which carriers are hitting their delivery targets. If you are struggling with the interface, ask Lazur to guide you through the setup process. It will wait for each click, helping you build your report step by step.

Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in your Mac notch. It does not click buttons for you, but it acts as a guide. When you are stuck on a formula, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask for help. Lazur will explain the syntax out loud. If you need to write a quick note about a shipment issue, hold fn and dictate your thoughts directly into Excel. It keeps your hands on the keyboard and your focus on the data.
